title: Commercial pitch: Dedicated GPU value mapping
content:
Purpose
This is a working commercial brief for sales and solutions to quickly map Redwood Dedicated into a buyer’s commercial evaluation. Focus: translate SLAs, isolation features, and throughput guarantees into concrete ROI and procurement language. Not a final legal artifact — use for discovery calls, presales, and procurement playbook inputs.

High-level thesis
Buyers don’t buy GPUs — they buy predictability for customer-facing AI features. Our value proposition: convert unpredictable variable cost and operational toil into a contractually-backed, capacity-guaranteed service that delivers predictable latency, throughput, and unit economics.

One-line pitch (for SDR/AE)
"Redwood Dedicated gives your team predictable inference throughput and isolation so product SLAs stay stable as usage scales — with contract guarantees and operational handoff for rapid production launches."

Key buyer personas and their priorities
- Platform/Infra Lead: capacity planning, predictable costs, tenant isolation, failover playbooks.
- ML/Prod Eng Lead: model performance parity with hosted, latency p99 targets, consistent KV-cache behavior across nodes.
- Procurement / Legal: contractual SLAs, remedies, export/security clauses, PoP.
- Security & Compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs and data residency.

Value mapping framework (how to quantify with customers)
1) Baseline: current variability cost
   - Ask: last 3 months peak TPS, median TPS, frequency of throttles or OOMs, token-unit spend.
   - Convert variability into a percentage uplift on cost-per-request and time-to-market risk.
2) Dedicated uplift: guaranteed capacity + reserved pricing
   - Map reserved GPU units to peak TPS and model family (e.g., 8x A100-80GB equiv -> X p95 tokens/s for Llama2-70b-like workload).
   - Translate to $/1000 effective inference tokens under expected concurrency.
3) SLA delta: incident frequency -> commercial remediation
   - Estimate avoided downtime minutes/year from fallback to Hosted or cross-region failover; convert to revenue-at-risk reduction or developer-hours saved.
4) Operational amortization
   - Time saved by not operating model infra (SRE/infra FTE months) -> $ savings.

Procurement-ready positioning bullets (what to put in an RFP response)
- Guaranteed throughput: committed TPU/GPU pool with documented mapping to model families and sequence-length assumptions.
- Isolation: tenant-level network segmentation, isolated queues, and dedicated nodes for enterprise workloads.
- SLA: uptime and latency SLOs with credit matrix (e.g., credits applied at monthly invoice for p99 latency breaches and availability).
- Capacity elasticity: contractual autoscale policies and burst pools for traffic spikes; service-level burst window defined.
- Data controls: VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, audit log exports, optional air-gapped calendar for on-prem packaging.

Competitive differentiation (notes for objection handling)
- Cloud-managed endpoints: cheaper entry price but opaque routing, noisy neighbors, and limited contractual throughput guarantees. We win when customers need predictable top-end performance and isolation.
- Self-hosted runtimes: often cheaper in pure $/GPU but requires teams to own failure modes, kernel selection, and capacity ops. We win on speed-to-production and transfer of operational risk.
- Single-vendor ML clouds: good integrations but limited openness around model variants and quantization tuning. We win on model flexibility + per-workload performance engineering.

Pricing anchors and negotiation levers
- Anchor on committed monthly GPU-equivalent units (not per-token). Show clear mapping: X committed units -> Y p95 throughput -> Z effective $/1M tokens.
- Offer tiered breach remedies: technical support SLAs, usage credits, or step-down pricing for sustained miss. Keep legal fallback simple (credits rather than complex indemnities) for faster procurement cycles.
- Flexibility: 3-month pilot with committed minimum transitioning into 12/24 month reserved contract with reduced per-unit price.

SLA and contract clause checklist (sales ops + legal)
- Define measurement methodology: telemetry sources for availability and p99 latency, who's the arbiter (Redwood Console + customer telemetry).
- Credit schedule: clearly state how credits are calculated and applied to invoices.
- Failure modes and remedies: capacity shortage, region outage, node-level hardware failure — outline remediation steps and timeboxes.
- Security & audit commitments: frequency of audits, logs retention, and access during incident investigations.
- Migration/fallback support: contract obligations to assist with rollbacks or temporary Hosted proxying during incidents.

Technical proof points to include in the commercial packet
- Benchmark table: model family -> committed GPU-equivalent -> expected p95 latency (50/128/512 tokens) -> throughput (tokens/s).
- Observability sample: example Console dashboard export showing per-token cost, p99 latency trend, and per-route utilization.
- Case vignette (anonymized): customer X reduced inference cost variance by 42% and removed 0.6 FTE of infra ops within 9 months.

Conversation scripts and objection handling (short)
- "Why not self-host?" -> "Self-hosting leaves you owning kernel and failure modes. Redwood Dedicated transfers those risks to us and gives a contractual runway to grow with predictable spend."
- "We need to see numbers first." -> "Let’s run a short 6–8 week sizing pilot: we drop a capacity mapping against a representative traffic trace and deliver an expected cost/throughput model you can take to procurement."
- "What if we need more capacity quickly?" -> "We have burst pools and explicit burst SLA windows; for sustained increases we convert incremental capacity to reserved units on a short ramp schedule."

Quick presales checklist (what to collect on the discovery call)
- Representative model(s) and typical sequence lengths.
- Recent 7/30/90 day peak and p95 concurrency.
- Current unit economics (cost per 1k tokens) and any fixed budgets.
- Security/region/residency constraints and any compliance packages required.

Next steps for the go-to-market team
- Create a short sales one-pager with the bench-mark table and a pilot offer template.
- Build a lightweight estimator sheet that maps committed units -> throughput -> $/1M tokens for the AE to run live in calls.
- Align with legal to finalize a credit-first SLA appendix to shorten procurement cycles.

Notes / open questions
- Need an agreed public mapping table between our named instances (e.g., RD-dedicated-xlarge) and industry GPU equivalents for procurement negotiation.
- Confirm standard burst pool size and default burst window for commercial offers.
- Validate the credit schedule with finance to ensure clear margin impact.

Author notes
Working draft — please add real benchmark rows and a downloadable estimator in the shared GTM drive. Use this doc for call scripts and presales briefings; update with field feedback after 3 live pilots.
